subject: Private GPU reserve + routing heuristics for sustained bursts

Subject: Private GPU sizing ask: sustained 600-800 qps bursts for pilot

Hi Jonas / Marissa / Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. Quick context: AcmeCloud is piloting a private VPC deployment of our conversational endpoint. Our preliminary traffic shows frequent windows of 10-20 minutes where QPS jumps to ~600-800 (mostly short requests, avg token length ~45). Baseline steady-state QPS is ~120.

Two asks to help procurement and infra sizing:
- A recommendation for a committed pool size + warm buffer to hit a 99th-percentile tail latency target of 250ms for generation paths during those 10-20m windows.
- A conservative routing/fallback heuristic if the warm pool drains (how quickly to spill to dedicated or hosted, and what fallback model fidelity we should accept).

I attached a single 48-hour sample extract we captured (acme_traffic_sample.csv). Please advise what extra signals you need.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Shah

Priya — thanks, this is actionable. High level I expect a two-layer approach: (1) commit to a steady base pool sized for median load, and (2) reserve a warm buffer configured for short bursts with fast warm-up + KV prefix priming.

Action items I propose:
1) Marissa: run a quick reserve-buffer model on the CSV and give a recommended buffer (% and absolute GPUs) and expected 99p latency curve.
2) Laura: propose a routing fallback ladder (same-region lower-cost models, cross-region fallback, hosted API overflow) and the SLO degradation plan.
3) Priya: confirm SLA tolerance for short-term fidelity reduction (are 20% slower p95s acceptable for 10 minutes? or do we need fidelity-first behavior).

If you can get Marissa's numbers today we can present to Acme procurement tomorrow.

Subject: Re: Private GPU sizing ask: sustained 600-800 qps bursts for pilot

TL;DR — baseline recommendation: commit to 72-GPU pool with a configurable warm buffer = 25% (~18 GPUs) for 10–20 minute bursts; fallback ladder documented below.

Notes and assumptions (from the attached reserve_buffer_model_v1.xlsx):
- Traffic profile: median concurrency ~45 QPS, 95p ~160, observed short-window surges to 700–820 with 40–50% of requests under 60 tokens.
- Model: we simulated a mixture of medium-length context (seq len 512) on A100-like capacity using our continuous-batching model. Key points:
  * Committed pool of 72 GPUs sustains steady-state median+buffered load with minimal queuing for typical token lengths.
  * Warm buffer sizing: 25% reserve (18 GPUs) yields an expected 99th-percentile tail latency <= 260ms under observed surge profile if KV cache is pre-warmed for active tenants.
  * If KV caching cannot be primed, add a 30–40% warm buffer or accept a p99 uplift of ~30% during first 2–3 minutes.

Fallback ladder (recommended):
1) Intra-VPC spill to lower-memory quantized variant (same-region) — retains fidelity ~95% and reduces per-token latency by ~12ms.
2) Cross-region fallback to Dedicated pool (if intra-VPC threshold exhausted) — added network RTT but CPU/GPU availability preserves throughput; use as second line for requests flagged non-sensitive.
3) Hosted API overflow (last resort) — route only non-sensitive or low-fidelity deprioritized requests; degrade generation settings (temp / max tokens) to conserve capacity.

Operational knobs:
- Fast warm-up: pre-allocate reserved kernels and keep a small pool of preforked processes so spin-up time < 20s.
- KV priming: request prefetch windows from client side for known conversational sessions.
- Egress: cap per-VM NIC to avoid tenant cross-talk; see network-egress-map.png.

I've attached the reserve model and the CSV slice we used. Numbers in the spreadsheet include sensitivity rows for 15/25/40% reserve. Pick a risk tolerance and we can finalize.

Attachments: reserve_buffer_model_v1.xlsx, acme_traffic_sample.csv
— Marissa

Subject: Re: Private GPU sizing ask: sustained 600-800 qps bursts for pilot

Good notes. A couple items I want captured before we hand to procurement:
1) Routing policy triggers — define clear headroom thresholds:
   - GREEN: pool utilization < 65% -> normal routing.
   - AMBER: 65–85% -> start KV cache priming, increase batch windows where latency SLA allows, spin up N warm GPUs (N = configured buffer step).
   - RED: > 85% -> initiate spill to fallback ladder in order (intra-VPC quantized variant -> cross-region dedicated -> hosted overflow).
2) SLAs for overflow: set explicit degradation: on first spill set quality-preserving mode (quantize weights, reduce sampling budget), on second spill allow fidelity drop up to 20% but maintain p95 <= 500ms.
3) Network constraints: confirm egress budget per-tenant and whether Acme allows cross-region fallbacks for regulated traffic. Benji from EdgeOps pointed out some cloud-provider egress caps that could throttle our overflow path (see network-egress-map.png).

Priya — can you confirm regulatory constraints (no cross-region for PII) and whether Acme will accept the proposed fidelity ladder?

— Laura
VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Benji Tan <benji.tan@edgeops.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private GPU sizing ask: sustained 600-800 qps bursts for pilot

All — thanks for the fast turnaround. Finalized plan we agreed to propose to Acme procurement:
- Commit: 72 GPUs (A100 equiv) in private VPC.
- Warm buffer: 25% (18 GPUs) with fast warm-up (target < 20s) and KV priming requirement.
- Routing: GREEN/AMBER/RED thresholds as Laura outlined; explicit fallback ladder for capacity preservation.
- Policy: cross-region fallback only for non-PII traffic (Priya please confirm), hosted overflow as last resort with fidelity caps.
- Procurement ask: include a one-time warm-up exercise (load test) and a 3-month trial with monthly usage review to tune buffer %.

I've attached the network-egress-map.png we discussed and the reserve model will go to the Acme shared drive (link above). Priya — if you confirm PII constraints we will convert this into a mutual action plan and hand to procurement.

Jonas
Director, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
